lots.title: Maintenance and extension of the Operational Windstorm Service
lots.description: Maintain and further develop the operational windstorm climate service under C3S, primarily designed to support the insurance and risk management sector. Ensure continued operational delivery, scientific robustness, and strategic extension of the Operational Windstorm Service, including preparation for ERA6, enhancement of derived indicators (return periods, cumulated precipitation), AI-based methods for storm detection and generative extension of statistics, geographic extension beyond Europe to Northern (and where feasible Southern) Hemisphere midlatitudes, maintenance and development of prototype applications and Jupyter notebooks, user engagement, co-designed online demonstrators, training, EQC liaison and L2 user support.
requirements: Maintain ongoing operational delivery, monitoring and troubleshooting of the CDS dataset 'Windstorm tracks and footprints derived from reanalysis over Europe between 1940 to present' (sis-european-wind-storm-reanalysis), including monthly updates as new ERA5 reanalysis data become available.

Maintain and further develop the two prototype applications associated with the windstorm dataset, ensuring they remain fully operational, are updated following dataset changes, and are promptly restored in coordination with C3S in the event of technical issues.
Maintain Jupyter Notebooks associated with the windstorm dataset for advanced and expert users.

Identify, diagnose and resolve issues affecting the datasets, CDS catalogue entries, documentation, underlying code and Jupyter Notebooks, including scientific completeness checks against known recent high-impact European windstorms.
Review, validate and where necessary correct post-processing and spatial filtering criteria applied to the ETC diagnostics so that high-impact European windstorms are not inadvertently excluded.
Assess the implications of the ETC diagnostics for use in climate assessment products, in particular contributions to the C3S European State of the Climate (ESOTC) report.

Explore, test and benchmark AI-based methods for identification, tracking and characterisation of extra-tropical cyclones and windstorms with the objective of reproducing the existing algorithm-based diagnostics; AI methods must be physically consistent, fully documented and rigorously evaluated against the current ERA5-based methodology before any operational implementation.
Provide Level-2 user support for windstorm products by responding to user queries escalated by the C3S User Support team.

Prepare migration of the CDS catalogue entry and associated workflows to ERA6, including targeted testing of storm detection, tracking and post-processing on initially available ERA6 data, and assessment of sensitivity to changes in resolution, model formulation and data availability.

Geographically extend the windstorm service from its current European domain to cover the entire Northern Hemisphere midlatitudes and, where technically and scientifically feasible, the Southern Hemisphere midlatitudes, ensuring methodological consistency with existing European products.
Add cumulated precipitation associated with windstorm events as a complementary hazard variable alongside wind gusts.

Introduce return period estimates for key variables relevant to windstorm risk, ensuring methodological consistency and suitability for risk assessment applications, recognising that insurance premiums are typically reviewed on an annual basis.

Develop and assess methodologies to enhance windstorm statistics for downstream use in risk and catastrophe modelling, including approaches such as UNSEEN-type resampling exploiting large physically consistent ensembles, generation of synthetic windstorm events, perturbation- or analogue-based approaches, and AI-based generative methods.

Benchmark proposed enhanced-statistics methodologies against the existing ERA5-based windstorm dataset, evaluate them for physical realism and statistical robustness, and document assumptions, limitations and suitability for downstream catastrophe modelling.

Develop and assess extra-tropical storm-related indicators suitable for both historical reanalysis (ERA5/ERA6) and climate projection datasets (CMIP / CORDEX), based on gridded or regional diagnostics such as exceedance metrics, spatial aggregates, persistence measures or footprint-based indicators; target ensembles include CMIP6 (or CMIP7 when available) over reference, near-term (e.g. 2021-2050) and end-century (e.g. 2071-2100) windows.

Ensure methodological consistency with the Copernicus Climate Change Service Atlas in terms of selected climate models, designed to remain robust under evolving background models and ensemble configurations.

Develop a user engagement strategy identifying relevant communities (insurance, reinsurance, EIOPA or equivalent policymakers, catastrophe modelling community), collecting requirements and supporting co-development of case studies and demonstrators.

Co-develop and deliver online demonstrators for case studies that demonstrate added value: regularly updated operational products with a visual component (e.g. graphical products or web applications), with the underlying datasets delivered to C3S via the CDS in a way that can be automatically maintained even after the contract ends; complete documentation of workflows and methodologies must be provided.

Co-design and deliver training and dissemination materials with champion users and ECMWF (interactive webinars, fact sheets, training events), and present the products at specific events agreed with ECMWF (one event per year expected); accommodate ad hoc requests to support ECMWF training, education and capacity-building activities including train-the-trainer events and MOOCs.
Liaise with the contractors in charge of the C3S Evaluation and Quality Control (EQC) component.
Set up and provide content (text, tools, materials developed under the contract) for a C3S website to create a continuously updated web presence for the service.
Ensure coordination and technical consistency with Lot 2 for joint windstorm/storm-surge products and related compound hazards (see Section 6).
Propose a coherent set of work packages and a deliverables plan addressing the technical tasks above, following the guidelines in Section 7.3.

lots.title: Maintenance and extension of operational storm surge products
lots.description: Ensure the continued operational delivery, scientific robustness and strategic extension of the C3S Operational Storm Surge Climate Service. Scope includes operationalising the storm-surge / extreme-sea-level product chain with NRT delivery and QA/QC, ERA6 preparation, AI-based method exploration for surrogate / emulation / post-processing, maintenance and evolution of statistical indicators (percentiles, return periods, confidence bounds), restructuring of the climate-projections component to a broad CMIP6/CMIP7 selection aligned with the C3S Atlas, plus training, L2 support, ESOTC contribution and website presence.
requirements: Maintain the existing storm-surge / extreme sea-level service: variables, formats, spatial and temporal coverage, and CDS interfaces; the maintenance requirement is defined in terms of products and functionality rather than a fixed underlying model implementation.

Operationalise the reanalysis-based storm surge product: generate an operational chain to update the current product with NRT delivery and ensure continuous operational delivery at least at the same quality and resolution as the current product, with timely restoration after issues.
Implement an operational update cycle, with updates at least monthly (or as agreed with ECMWF/C3S), to incorporate newly available reanalysis data and keep the catalogue current.

Implement QA/QC procedures appropriate for operational dissemination: consistency checks, completeness checks, outlier detection, metadata validation, and verification against known historical high-water events where feasible.
Maintain and update CDS catalogue entries, documentation and user guidance so that changes are traceable and reproducible.

If proposing alternative modelling frameworks or updated model versions, ensure outputs are scientifically equivalent or improved, fully document methodological changes and assess impacts on historical consistency, uncertainty and interpretation; any underlying-model change is subject to scientific validation, benchmarking against the existing products and ECMWF/C3S approval prior to operational adoption.

Prepare the storm surge product chain for ERA6, including impact assessment on forcing fields, resolution and availability; targeted 'early ERA6' end-to-end testing (forcing → modelling/post-processing → delivery); and a documented sensitivity assessment with a migration plan for operational adoption when ERA6 is available at scale.

Explore AI-based methods for generation, emulation, acceleration or post-processing of storm surge and extreme sea-level products (surrogate/emulation models, AI-assisted bias correction or downscaling, hybrid physics+ML approaches); methods must be physically consistent, scientifically justified, rigorously evaluated against existing physics-based products and assessed for robustness, stability and operational suitability — without compromising operational continuity or reliability.

Maintain the indicator generation chain (percentiles, return periods, confidence bounds for total water levels and surge levels), including downstream processing, delivery, validation and documentation within the C3S operational context.

Ensure indicators remain consistent across updates (versioning, methodological traceability, backward compatibility where possible); document methods, assumptions, limitations and uncertainty treatment (extreme-value methodology, confidence intervals, sensitivity to record length); expand indicators as needed by the user community.

Restructure the climate-projections component (currently a HighResMIP CMIP6 subset) so that storm-surge / sea-level indicators can be produced and assessed from a broad selection of CMIP6 simulations available in the CDS up to 2100 — and CMIP7 simulations when available — using a design robust to evolving model availability and ensemble composition.
Align the projections component with the C3S Atlas philosophy: transparent model selection rules, consistent periods/scenarios, robust ensemble statistics and reproducible processing.

Define and document a model/ensemble selection strategy (eligibility criteria, scenario coverage, near-term / mid-century / end-century temporal windows, handling of multiple realizations) and a consistent approach for ensemble aggregation and uncertainty characterisation (e.g. model spread, internal variability proxies, robustness metrics consistent with Atlas practices).

Ensure methodological consistency and traceability between historical reanalysis indicators (ERA5/ERA6) and future indicators derived from CMIP ensembles, with clear separation of drivers (mean sea level contribution vs surge/tide variability) where relevant.
Co-define indicator design with a subset of users / use cases together with C3S.
Contribute to coordination efforts with Lot 1 and ensure technical consistency for relevant joint windstorm / storm-surge products and related compound hazards (Section 6).
Provide updated training and example workflows (e.g. notebooks demonstrating retrieval, visualisation, detrending, percentile/return-period calculations and interpretation).
Provide Level-2 user support when escalated by the C3S User Support function (Jira ticketing and/or user forum, single email contact, KPI 85% L2 tickets resolved within 15 business days).
Set up and provide content (text, tools, materials developed under the contract) for a C3S website to create a continuously updated web presence for the service.
Contribute to ESOTC report writing if relevant products are included in a section (Section 7.6).
Propose a coherent set of work packages and a deliverables plan addressing the technical tasks above, following the guidelines in Section 7.3.

warnings.message: The tender specification document does not enumerate explicit CPV codes per lot. CPV 73000000-2 (Research and development services and related consultancy services) was inferred from the notice main_category supplied as cross-reference context. Both lots concern R&D / scientific services for the Copernicus Climate Change Service.

Pre-existing notice title is 'C3S2_413_bis Lot 2 Maintenance and Extension of C3S Windstorm and Storm Surge Services' which suggests a single Lot 2. The tender specification document explicitly defines TWO distinct lots (Lot 1: Windstorm Service; Lot 2: Storm Surge products) under ITT C3S2_413_bis and Section 3 confirms 'Tenderers are invited to submit their Tenders for either one or both Lots.' Both lots have therefore been emitted authoritatively from the document; the notice metadata appears to have a confusing title but the underlying notice_lots rows for lot_number 1 and 2 are consistent with the document.

Section 6 'Joint products and cross-Lot coordination (Lot 1 & Lot 2)' describes joint windstorm/storm-surge products. These are NOT a separate lot — Section 6 is a coordination obligation flowing back into both Lot 1 and Lot 2. They have been incorporated into each lot's requirements (cross-Lot coordination requirement) rather than emitted as a third lot.
evidence_refs: Volume II §6 Joint products and cross-Lot coordination
